newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina won't meet budget deadline - Senate.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina won't meet budget deadline - Senate.

text.p: The North Carolina Senate has acknowledged the state probably will not have a budget agreement by the start of the new fiscal year on July 1, and passed a bill continuing funding at current levels.
The Senate voted 47-2 Thursday to extend this year's spending levels until Aug 1. The House was scheduled to consider the bill on Monday.
House and Senate leaders have been deadlocked for two weeks on their $11.4 billion budget proposals. They remain at odds over Medicaid and welfare funding.
Both chambers have agreed to raise teacher pay and fund the Smart Start program for early childhood education.
The Senate plan would use $40 million from the Medicaid Trust Fund for Medicaid-related programs, and $23 million of federal funds for Smart Start.
The Republican-controlled House would pull $25 million from the Medicaid Trust Fund for Medicaid-related programs, and allocate $22 million for Smart Start from the general fund.
